newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Rival parties clash in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Rival parties clash in Cambodia.

text.p: Supporters of the two main parties in Cambodia's coalition government have clashed outside the country's second largest city, police and soldiers said on Friday.
They said the supporters of the two parties clashed on Friday after two royalists were detained by their rivals at Rengsei, 20 km (12 miles) east of Battambang.

"There is big fighting between FUNCINPEC and the CPP this morning because last night the CPP arrested two members of FUNCINPEC at the FUNCINPEC office in Rengsei commune," a senior FUNCINPEC military officer said.
"Now we will send more troops to them," said the officer, who asked not to be named. He would not give a figure for the number of reinforcements.

The incident appeared to reflect the deteriorating relations between the royalist FUNCINPEC and the Cambodian People's Party (CPP) and their leaders, co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh (FUNCINPEC) and Hun Sen (CPP).
The two are former battlefield foes who formed an uneasy alliance after U.N.-run elections in 1993.
But the governor of Battambang province, CPP member Ung Samy, told Reuters by telephone there had been no fighting on Thursday night or Friday.
"There's no fighting at all... Don't believe it, it's just a rumour," he said.
The clashes, if confirmed, would represent the most serious escalation of a feud between Battambang Governor Ung Samy and his deputy, FUNCINPEC's Serei Kosal, analysts said.
Relations between Ung Samy and his deputy, Serei Kosal, plummeted in November after clashes between the CPP and FUNCINPEC in the province left several people wounded.
The governor and deputy governor were told to cooperate in holding local and general elections due by the end of the year, but ill-feeling has continued to simmer amid fresh reports of violence.
